items.title: Stocks give back gains as Anthropic dips below IPO price
items.summary:
Hosts Julie Hyman and Jake Conley, joined on the couch by Barron's markets reporter Jacob Sonenshine, tackle the top stories of the day. Including futures sliding after Monday's biggest rally since April 2025, Anthropic briefly trading below its $83 IPO price, a Wall Street Journal report that the U.S. is preparing new tariffs on China and dozens of other countries, and whether Jensen Huang's return leaves Nvidia owing a favor to the White House.

The team is joined by Seaport Research Partners senior analyst Jay Goldberg and Creative Strategies CEO and principal analyst Ben Bajarin to discuss what Jensen Huang needs to tell shareholders, the competitive threat from Broadcom and AMD, and whether Nvidia's financing of neoclouds is a wobbly foundation. The show closes on Strategy trading below the value of its Bitcoin, Sanofi's $41 billion deal for Insmed, and a strong day for retail earnings from Best Buy, Dollar Tree, Dick's, Abercrombie, and Kohl's.

items.title: Walmart’s Robot Warehouse Partner Symbotic Just Had Its First Profitable Year
items.summary: Symbotic finally posted a full year in the black and locked in a decade of Walmart work, yet investors barely reacted. The real story sits in what the headline profit leaves out and what must happen next.

items.title: Retail stocks surge into Black Friday amid earnings beats
items.summary: Investing.com - U.S. retail stocks are rallying broadly Tuesday as a rotation out of AI and technology names accelerates into the holiday season, with Kohl’s Corp (NYSE:KSS) leading the group with a 14.2% surge after its most recent quarter beat consensus by $1.76 per share. The State Street® SPDR® S&P® Retail ETF (NYSE:XRT) is gaining 1.84% alongside its largest constituents as money flows out of technology and into consumer-facing value plays with Black Friday three days away.

items.title: Consumer Mood Improves Into Holidays, But Risks Loom
items.summary:
US consumer confidence surged in November to the highest in nearly two years as Americans grew more optimistic about the economy and the job market. 
Seema Shah, VP: Insights at Sensor Tower, discusses consumer trends and spending ahead of Black Friday and the holidays.
